_comment: Shared test vectors for the running-order NUMBERING rule (T158).
runningOrderNumbers(entries) -> a number (1-based) per entry, or null.
THE RULE, stated once: a number belongs only to a MAIN-ORDER SONG — a song that is NOT on-call and
NOT an intermission. An on-call (bench) song or an intermission carries no number and NEVER shifts the
number of the entry after it. So '7' means the 7th main song on the printed sheet, in the Stage drawer,
and in the Studio editor alike.
Three surfaces run these SAME vectors as a test so they cannot silently diverge: TroubaStage (Kotlin,
drawerRows), TroubaStudio (TS, SetlistDetail), TroubaCore (Go, the T158 export document). Each maps its
own model to (kind, onCall) and compares to `expected`. Values are hand-derived from the rule, not
emitted by any implementation, so an off-by-one or a bench/intermission that shifts the count fails.
kind is 'song' or 'intermission'; onCall applies only to a song. expected uses null for no number.
Intermission cases are forward-looking (T153): the numbering must already be correct when it lands.

cases.name: a trailing on-call song is unnumbered
an on-call song mid-list does NOT shift the song after it
an intermission between songs 2 and 3 leaves the next song reading 3
a leading intermission does not consume the number 1
intermission and on-call together, both unnumbered
